activities.title: Establish customer feedback review
activities.description: Create a practical way to understand how customers experience delivered products or services and how that information should influence quality decisions.
activities.objective: Establish a proportionate customer-perception review method that turns useful feedback into visible decisions and improvement inputs.
activities.why_it_matters: Customer perception can change before a formal complaint appears, so broader feedback helps the organization see recurring strengths, friction, and emerging risk.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Identify useful feedback sources such as complaints, compliments, surveys, scorecards, returns, service issues, repeat business, cancellations, meetings, delivery feedback, portals, and documented informal feedback.
2. Assign an owner and choose a review interval suited to the organization's size, risk, and customer relationships.
3. Distinguish individual issues from recurring patterns and record the reasoning behind important conclusions.
4. Route issues into the existing NCR or CAPA workflow when their significance warrants it.
5. Retain review decisions, actions, and follow-up expectations.
6. Check whether the feedback method remains useful and adjust it when experience shows a gap.
activities.expected_output: A usable customer-perception review mechanism with defined sources, ownership, review cadence, trend handling, and action routing.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include a feedback-source inventory, review record, trend summary, customer meeting note, issue referral, decision log, or method review.
activities.success_criteria: Relevant customer feedback is gathered from more than one appropriate source where available, recurring trends can be distinguished from individual events, and decisions or actions are retained without requiring one universal survey or metric.
activities.responsible_role: Customer Service Owner with Quality Manager

activities.title: Establish the quality KPI system
activities.description: Build a small, useful measurement and review system for QMS and process performance rather than collecting metrics without a decision purpose.
activities.objective: Define how selected quality and process indicators are measured, interpreted, reviewed, and connected to action.
activities.why_it_matters: Reliable measures help the organization notice performance change, test whether controls work, and focus improvement effort where it matters.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Decide what performance needs monitoring and why each selected measure supports a real decision.
2. Define the metric, source, owner, calculation, baseline where useful, target or limit, expected direction, and review cadence.
3. Establish how results are reviewed, trended, interpreted, and escalated.
4. Record actions or decisions when results move outside the intended range or reveal a pattern.
5. Review whether each metric remains useful and retire or change ineffective measures.
6. Keep the set proportionate; a small useful set is preferable to measuring everything.
activities.expected_output: A proportionate quality KPI system with defined measures, sources, ownership, calculations, review rules, and action triggers.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include a KPI definition, data-source note, calculation example, baseline, target record, measurement history, trend review, escalation, or metric review decision.
activities.success_criteria: Selected measures have clear purpose and ownership, results can be reproduced from their source, review decisions are visible, and ineffective measures can be changed without weakening oversight.
activities.responsible_role: Data / KPI Owner with Quality Manager

activities.title: Protect quality data integrity
activities.description: Define proportionate controls so quality and performance information remains understandable, traceable, and fit for the decisions that depend on it.
activities.objective: Establish ownership and review practices that protect meaningful quality data from accidental distortion and unexplained change.
activities.why_it_matters: A decision is only as useful as the context and trustworthiness of the data behind it, especially when trends drive action.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Identify important quality data sources and assign owners for collection, review, correction, and retention.
2. Document calculation logic, time period, version, and context needed to interpret significant measures or results.
3. Check completeness, consistency, traceability, and reconciliation needs proportionate to use and risk.
4. Define how errors are corrected, explained, approved where needed, and kept distinguishable from original results.
5. Limit inappropriate changes while keeping legitimate operational correction possible.
6. Review data controls when a significant decision, discrepancy, or process change exposes a weakness.
activities.expected_output: A practical quality-data integrity method covering sources, ownership, interpretation, correction, review, and retention context.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include a data-source register, ownership assignment, calculation definition, reconciliation, correction record, review checklist, version context, or discrepancy decision.
activities.success_criteria: Decision-makers can identify where meaningful quality data came from, understand how it was calculated and bounded in time, distinguish corrections, and have reasonable confidence that it was not unintentionally distorted.
activities.responsible_role: Data / KPI Owner with Process Owners

activities.title: Control nonconforming outputs
activities.description: Establish immediate operational controls for an output that does not meet defined criteria, whether the output is a product, service result, material, deliverable, or process result.
activities.objective: Prevent an affected output from unintended use, release, delivery, or continued processing until an authorized disposition or correction is decided.
activities.why_it_matters: Fast identification and containment reduce the chance that an unsuitable result reaches a customer or moves further through the operation.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Define how a potentially nonconforming output is identified and its status made visible.
2. Apply proportionate containment, segregation, access, hold, or equivalent control.
3. Assign disposition authority and define correction, rework, concession, deviation, or rejection routes where relevant.
4. Verify the result after correction before releasing or continuing the work.
5. Notify the customer or affected parties when the situation requires it.
6. Retain the disposition and verification result and refer a wider issue into NCR management when appropriate.
activities.expected_output: An immediate nonconforming-output control method with status, containment, disposition authority, verification, and communication rules.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include a hold/status record, containment action, disposition decision, rework approval, verification result, concession, or customer notification.
activities.success_criteria: Affected outputs are identifiable and controlled before unintended use, authorized disposition is clear, correction is verified, and the response fits physical, digital, and service contexts.

activities.title: Manage nonconformities
activities.description: Create a consistent record and follow-up method for significant nonconformities from outputs, processes, audits, customers, suppliers, monitoring, or QMS failures.
activities.objective: Give the organization a proportionate workflow to record, evaluate, assign, follow up, and close nonconformities with a clear rationale.
activities.why_it_matters: A controlled NCR record keeps immediate correction, significance decisions, deeper analysis, and closure evidence from becoming disconnected.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Record what happened, its source, context, and affected scope.
2. Evaluate significance using impact, recurrence, risk, and available facts.
3. Assign an owner and capture immediate correction or containment.
4. Decide whether cause analysis or corrective action is warranted rather than applying either automatically.
5. Track actions, verification, and relevant links to risks, audits, customer issues, or suppliers.
6. Retain the closure rationale and reopen or escalate when the issue is not adequately resolved.
activities.expected_output: A proportionate nonconformity management workflow with source, significance, ownership, action, follow-up, and closure rationale.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include an NCR record, significance review, containment link, owner assignment, action history, verification note, closure rationale, or escalation decision.
activities.success_criteria: Significant nonconformities are traceable from occurrence through decision and follow-up, minor issues are handled proportionately, and closure does not depend on automatically creating an RCA or CAPA.

activities.title: Apply root-cause analysis
activities.description: Use structured cause analysis when recurrence, severity, customer impact, systemic risk, ineffective correction, or uncertainty makes deeper understanding worthwhile.
activities.objective: Establish a disciplined way to distinguish symptoms, contributing conditions, and credible underlying causes before deciding on further action.
activities.why_it_matters: Cause analysis is useful when it prevents recurrence or improves a decision, but forcing it onto every issue creates paperwork without better understanding.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Define when an issue warrants cause analysis using severity, recurrence, impact, risk, uncertainty, or prior ineffectiveness.
2. State the problem accurately and gather relevant evidence before choosing a method.
3. Use a suitable approach such as 5 Whys, fishbone, fault tree, process mapping, barrier analysis, or comparison.
4. Test the reasoning against facts and identify contributing or systemic causes where supported.
5. Record assumptions, limits, participants, and the rationale for the conclusion.
6. Link the conclusion to correction, corrective action, improvement, or a decision not to proceed.
activities.expected_output: A proportionate cause-analysis method with trigger criteria, evidence, reasoning, conclusion, and action linkage.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include an analysis record, evidence list, selected method, causal test, contributing-factor review, conclusion, or linkage to an NCR or CAPA.
activities.success_criteria: Cause analysis is used when warranted, the problem and evidence are clear, conclusions are supported rather than blame-based, and the selected method fits the issue.

activities.title: Verify corrective-action effectiveness
activities.description: Connect a validated cause to planned action, implementation, and a later effectiveness review before treating a corrective action as complete.
activities.objective: Establish a corrective-action cycle that can show whether the response reduced recurrence or achieved its intended result.
activities.why_it_matters: Completing an action does not prove that it worked; separating implementation from effectiveness protects the QMS from cosmetic closure.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Link the corrective action to the issue and cause it is intended to address.
2. Define the action owner, due date, resources, and effects on documents, training, changes, or related controls.
3. Implement the action and retain objective completion information.
4. Define an effectiveness method and wait long enough for the relevant result to be observable.
5. Review evidence against the intended outcome and decide whether to close, reopen, or reassess.
6. Feed lessons into improvement, risk, training, or other QMS processes when useful.
activities.expected_output: A corrective-action and effectiveness-review method that distinguishes correction, action implementation, result verification, and closure.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include a cause link, action plan, implementation record, updated control or training record, effectiveness measure, review decision, or reopen rationale.
activities.success_criteria: Actions address a stated cause, implementation and effectiveness are separately visible, evidence is sufficient for the timing and risk, and ineffective action leads to reassessment rather than automatic closure.

activities.title: Maintain the continual-improvement pipeline
activities.description: Maintain a visible and prioritized way to capture improvement opportunities that may arise from performance, feedback, audits, risks, operations, or leadership review.
activities.objective: Turn useful improvement ideas and lessons into evaluated, assigned, measured, and transparently closed or deferred work.
activities.why_it_matters: Continual improvement is broader than corrective action, so useful opportunities should remain visible even when no nonconformity exists.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Capture improvement inputs from KPI trends, feedback, employee ideas, audits, suppliers, NCR/CAPA lessons, risks, management review, and process analysis.
2. Evaluate value, urgency, effort, risk, and likely outcome.
3. Prioritize and assign an owner with an expected result or review point.
4. Implement the improvement and measure its result when measurement is meaningful.
5. Retain learning, decisions, and dependencies.
6. Close, defer, or reject the item transparently with a reason and revisit trigger where useful.
activities.expected_output: A prioritized continual-improvement pipeline with captured sources, decisions, owners, actions, results, and transparent disposition.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include an improvement opportunity, prioritization note, action record, result measure, lesson learned, deferral decision, or management review link.
activities.success_criteria: Improvement inputs are visible beyond CAPA, priorities and ownership are understandable, results or reasons are retained, and proportionality prevents every idea from becoming a formal corrective action.

activities.title: Establish the internal audit program
activities.description: Establish a planned and objective internal audit program that evaluates whether QMS arrangements are implemented and operating as intended using objective evidence.
activities.objective: Define a risk-informed audit program with scope, criteria, competent auditors, evidence sampling, findings, reporting, and follow-up.
activities.why_it_matters: A useful internal audit provides an evidence-based view of operation and improvement needs rather than acting as a checklist or attendance exercise.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Define the audit universe, scope, objectives, criteria, and reference basis.
2. Set frequency using risk, performance, history, changes, and prior findings rather than a fixed annual rule for everything.
3. Assign competent auditors and protect independence or objectivity for the activity being reviewed.
4. Plan sampling and gather objective evidence from relevant records, interviews, and observation.
5. Record findings, conclusions, reports, and responsible follow-up.
6. Review completion and response effectiveness through the existing audit and improvement workflows.
activities.expected_output: A practical internal audit program with planned scope, objective evidence, competent and suitably independent auditors, findings, reporting, and follow-up.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include an audit program, scope and criteria, auditor assignment, plan, sample record, working notes, finding, report, follow-up, or closure review.
activities.success_criteria: Audits are planned from risk and experience, use objective evidence, distinguish findings from checklist completion, preserve objectivity, and produce traceable follow-up without being confused with an external audit.

activities.title: Prepare management review inputs and decisions
activities.description: Establish an ongoing leadership review of QMS performance and conditions that produces decisions, priorities, resources, and assigned follow-up.
activities.objective: Connect meaningful QMS information to leadership evaluation and recorded decisions that influence the operating system.
activities.why_it_matters: A management review is valuable when leaders evaluate what the information means and decide what should change, not merely when a meeting or slide deck exists.
activities.implementation_steps:
1. Define the review rhythm, participants, owners, and practical preparation route.
2. Gather useful information such as prior actions, context changes, feedback, objectives and KPI results, process results, NCR/CAPA, audit results, supplier performance, resources, risks, improvements, and major changes.
3. Present information with enough context for leadership evaluation and prioritization.
4. Record decisions, resource actions, improvement actions, QMS changes, owners, due dates, and follow-up expectations.
5. Link resulting actions back to the relevant QMS records and review their status.
6. Adjust the inputs and review method when leadership decisions show that the information is incomplete or not useful.
activities.expected_output: An ongoing management-review method with meaningful inputs, leadership decisions, priorities, resources, owners, due dates, and follow-up.
activities.evidence_expectations: Examples may include an input summary, performance trend, action status, leadership decision, resource assignment, change decision, meeting record, or follow-up review.
activities.success_criteria: Leadership evaluates relevant QMS information, decisions and actions are recorded with ownership and timing, and review outputs feed the operating QMS rather than stopping at attendance or minutes.
